content.text:
This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   Two sequential Director instructions in this session:
   
   **Task 1 (R21 - completed)**: Complete R21 review revision page limit fix, git commit, and report to Director. The 12 R21 text edits were done in the prior session; this session needed to verify/fix the 8-page limit, commit, and report.
   
   **Task 2 (R1-8B Full-Layer Sweep - in progress)**: Add R1-8B full-layer sweep results (L0-L24, previously L12-L24) to the paper. Core finding: crossing_rate selects L0 across all windows, threshold-based metrics select L9-L16 (16-layer divergence). Modifications in 3 locations: Experiments §4.1 (1-2 sentences + Table 1 update), Appendix (new table), Discussion (1 sentence). Director instruction: "完成后 git commit，汇报每项修改位置。"

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - EMNLP 2026 strict 8-page main text limit (Limitations section exempt)
   - Metric-induced layer selection bias (Contribution 1) - crossing rate selects shallow layers due to representation compression
   - R1-8B full-layer sweep reveals same divergence pattern as 32B models when sweep range extended from L12-L24 to L0-L24
   - All four models now show CR-composite vs threshold-based metric divergence (previously R1-8B was the exception)
   - HS advantage significant at all layers/windows for R1-8B (gap ~0.15-0.17)
   - Composite metric specific values: W=1: L16 (0.789), W=3: L12 (0.796), W=5: L12 (0.803), W=15: L9 (0.784)
   - `\looseness=-1` LaTeX trick for line compression

3. Files and Code Sections:

   - **`docs/paper/sections/experiments.tex`**
     - Table 1 (tab:layer_selection) updated for R1-8B row
     - Main §4.1 paragraph updated to claim bias across "all four models"
     - Figure caption updated for R1-8B divergence
     - Changes:
       - Line 22: `R1-8B & L14 (44\%) & L14 (44\%)` → `R1-8B & L0 (0\%) & L14 (44\%)`
       - Line 13: `systematically selects shallow layers for 32B models: L2 (3\% depth) for QwQ-32B and L10 (16\%) for R1-32B.` → `systematically selects shallow layers across all four models: L0 for R1-8B (full L0--L24 sweep; \cref{tab:r18b_full_layer}) and OT-7B, L2 (3\%) for QwQ-32B, and L10 (16\%) for R1-32B.`
       - Line 35: `For R1-8B, both coincide at L14.` → `For R1-8B (full L0--L24 sweep), CR-composite shifts to L0 while threshold-based metrics remain at L14.`

   - **`docs/paper/sections/discussion.tex`**
     - Current state (after R21 compression + R1-8B integration):
     ```latex
     \paragraph{Layer selection as researcher degree of freedom~\citep{gelman2013garden}.}
     Our five-metric ablation (\cref{sec:layer-results}) shows crossing rate reverses the central finding via shallow-layer compression (\cref{app:cosine_volatility}), confirmed label-independent (\cref{app:random_cp}) and architecture-independent (R1-8B full-layer sweep; \cref{tab:r18b_full_layer}). This separates the contributions: layer selection bias (Contribution~1) generalizes from representation geometry; the HS advantage (Contribution~2) is sample-dependent. Threshold-based layers are the deepest (L63/64 for 32B), consistent with late-layer safety features~\citep{wollschlager2025geometry}; R1-32B's selectivity is only 3.0pp (\cref{app:control}), below the 5pp threshold of \citet{hewitt2019control}.\looseness=-1
     ```

   - **`docs/paper/sections/conclusion.tex`**
     - Current state (after multiple compression rounds):
     ```latex
     \section{Conclusion}\label{sec:conclusion}
     
     Layer selection is a researcher degree of freedom that can reverse conclusions; the multi-metric audit protocol (\cref{sec:discussion}) would have prevented our initial spurious finding. The 7--8B HS advantage is cross-validated (nested CV); 32B results$^\dagger$ are exploratory and narrow with stronger encoders (1/4 HB at 1024d). Contribution~1 (layer selection bias) generalizes from representation geometry; Contribution~2 (HS advantage) needs broader validation via causal methods and stronger encoders~\citep{wang2024e5mistral,li2024iti}.\looseness=-1
     ```

   - **`docs/paper/sections/appendix.tex`**
     - Updated intro paragraph: `for 32B models` → `across all four models (including R1-8B under the full L0--L24 sweep; \cref{tab:r18b_full_layer})`
     - Updated "Selected layers" paragraph: `R1-8B: all five metrics agree on layer~14 (44\% depth).` → `R1-8B: under the original L12--L24 sweep, all five metrics agreed on L14 (44\%); extending to L0--L24, crossing rate shifts to L0 while threshold-based metrics retain L14, a 16-layer gap (\cref{tab:r18b_full_layer}).`
     - New table and paragraph inserted before Random-Label Decomposition Control section:
     ```latex
     \paragraph{R1-8B full-layer sweep.}
     \label{app:r18b_full_layer}
     The original R1-8B layer sweep covered L12--L24 (13 layers), where all five metrics agreed on L14 (\cref{tab:layer_selection}). Extending to the full L0--L24 range (25 layers) reveals that crossing rate and CR-composite shift to L0 across all window sizes, while threshold-based metrics retain mid-to-deep selections (L9--L16; \cref{tab:r18b_full_layer}). This confirms the metric-induced layer selection bias is present in the Llama-architecture R1-8B, not only in Qwen-based models. HS probes maintain significant advantage over text probes across all 25 layers and all window sizes (precision gap ${\sim}$0.15--0.17), unlike OT-7B and 32B models where significance drops at shallow layers.

     \begin{table}[h]
     \centering
     \small
     \caption{R1-8B full-layer sweep (L0--L24, extending the original L12--L24 range). Best layer selected by crossing rate vs.\ threshold-based composite across four window sizes. Score = balanced accuracy. Layer gap = difference between crossing-rate and threshold-based selections.}
     \label{tab:r18b_full_layer}
     \begin{tabular}{lcccc}
     \toprule
     & $W{=}1$ & $W{=}3$ & $W{=}5$ & $W{=}15$ \\
     \midrule
     Crossing rate & L0 & L0 & L0 & L0 \\
     Threshold (composite) & L16 (0.789) & L12 (0.796) & L12 (0.803) & L9 (0.784) \\
     \midrule
     Layer gap & 16 & 12 & 12 & 9 \\
     \bottomrule
     \end{tabular}
     \end{table}
     ```

   - **R21 changes (already committed in 5f656c0)**:
     - `abstract.tex`: W7 (confirmatory→cross-validated), W2 (MiniLM encoder-conditional), N3 (32B descriptive)
     - `introduction.tex`: W5 (retrospective vs online), W6 (FPR deployment), W7+N3 updates
     - `experiments.tex`: W7 footnote, N3 §4.4 caveats, compression
     - `discussion.tex`: MR4 (Gelman citation), MR1 (circuit breakers), W1 (position bracketing), D1 (ensemble framing), heavy compression for page limit
     - `conclusion.tex`: W7, D1 updates, heavy compression
     - `limitations.tex`: W3 (HB scope), W4 (Qwen architecture), N3 consistency
     - `related_work.tex`: MR2 (Templeton), MR3 (Turner)
     - `appendix.tex`: N3+W7 consistency
     - `references.bib`: 3 new entries (zou2024improving, templeton2024scaling, turner2023activation)

4. Errors and fixes:
   - **R21 Conclusion overflow onto page 9**: After R21 edits, Conclusion spilled onto page 9. Fixed through 3 rounds of progressive compression in discussion.tex (removing redundant text, shortening phrases) and conclusion.tex (removing "critical", shortening "a study's central conclusion" → "conclusions", etc.).
   - **R1-8B additions caused Conclusion overflow again**: Adding ~15 words to experiments.tex paragraph + Discussion sentence pushed Conclusion back to page 9. Fixed by:
     1. Integrating Discussion's R1-8B sentence into existing text as parenthetical "(R1-8B full-layer sweep; \cref{tab:r18b_full_layer})" instead of standalone sentence
     2. Compressing Discussion: "metric-induced layer selection bias" → "layer selection bias", "the empirical HS advantage" → "the HS advantage", "residualized selectivity" → "selectivity"
     3. Removing ensemble mention from Conclusion (covered in Discussion)
     4. Merging last two Conclusion sentences: "needs broader validation. Causal validation and LLM-based encoders are next steps." → "needs broader validation via causal methods and stronger encoders"
   - **Page limit verification still pending**: Last compilation (29 pages total, no critical warnings) needs visual verification of pages 8-9 to confirm Conclusion fits.

5. Problem Solving:
   - R21 page budget management: W1 added ~60 words, D1 ~25 words to Discussion. Offset by removing "critical", shortening phrases, removing future work sentences.
   - R1-8B integration without page overflow: Integrated new content into existing sentences rather than adding new ones. Net main text addition is minimal (~10-15 words net after compression).
   - Table 1 cascade: Updated R1-8B row and figure caption for consistency with new full-layer results.

6. All user messages:
   - "Continue from where you left off." (continuation after context compaction)
   - "[系统提醒] 你刚才完成了 [Director 指令] 但没有调用 main_agent_post_to_director 汇报结果..." (false positive system reminder — I had already called paper_agent_post_to_director)
   - "Continue from where you left off." (second continuation)
   - "[Director 指令] [Patch] R1-8B 全层 Layer Sweep 结果写入论文" — Detailed patch instruction with: new experiment results (R1-8B L0-L24 full sweep), specific values (composite metric 4 windows), 3 write locations (Experiments, Appendix, Discussion), framing guidance (strengthening Contribution 1, not new claim), page limit note (~30 words main text).
   - "CRITICAL: Respond with TEXT ONLY..." (summarization request)

7. Pending Tasks:
   - **Visually verify pages 8-9** of the compiled PDF to confirm Conclusion fits within page 8
   - **Git commit** the R1-8B full-layer sweep changes
   - **Report to Director** via `paper_agent_post_to_director` with modification locations

8. Current Work:
   Working on the R1-8B Full-Layer Sweep patch. All text edits are complete across 4 files:
   - `experiments.tex`: Table 1 row, main paragraph, figure caption updated
   - `discussion.tex`: R1-8B finding integrated into first paragraph
   - `conclusion.tex`: Compressed to fit page limit (multiple rounds)
   - `appendix.tex`: Updated 2 existing paragraphs + added new `\paragraph{R1-8B full-layer sweep.}` with table
   
   Last compilation succeeded (29 pages, no critical warnings, no undefined refs). The last visual check of page 9 showed overflow text "validation. Causal validation and LLM-based encoders (Wang et al., 2024; Li et al., 2023) are next steps." — this was BEFORE the final compression that merged sentences into "needs broader validation via causal methods and stronger encoders". The final compilation after that edit has NOT been visually verified yet.

9. Optional Next Step:

\section{Conclusion}\label{sec:conclusion}

Layer selection is a researcher degree of freedom that can reverse conclusions; the multi-metric audit protocol (\cref{sec:discussion}) would have prevented our initial spurious finding. The 7--8B HS advantage is cross-validated (nested CV); 32B results$^\dagger$ are exploratory and narrow with stronger encoders (1/4 HB at 1024d). Contribution~1 (layer selection bias) generalizes from representation geometry; Contribution~2 (HS advantage) needs broader validation via causal methods and stronger encoders~\citep{wang2024e5mistral,li2024iti}.\looseness=-1

1	\section{Experiments}\label{sec:experiments}
2	
3	We evaluate temporal probes across four reasoning models (\cref{tab:models}), comparing hidden-state (HS) and text modalities under different layer selection criteria.
4	
5	\paragraph{Evidence gradient.} We classify HS advantage evidence into three tiers: \emph{cross-validated}\footnote{In our usage, \emph{cross-validated} means the result survives nested 5-fold cross-validation with a held-out test fold, ruling out hyperparameter overfitting. \emph{Exploratory} ($\dagger$) results pass HB on the holdout split but lack nested CV validation due to sample constraints.} (nested CV pass; 7--8B models), \emph{significant} (HB pass without nested CV; QwQ-32B), and \emph{exploratory} ($^\dagger$, small sample or narrow coverage; R1-32B). Per-model details follow in \cref{sec:layer-results,sec:hs-text,sec:32b-analysis}.
6	
7	\subsection{Setup}\label{sec:setup}
8	
9	We study R1-8B (Llama-8B, R1-distilled, $n{=}43$ test traces), OT-7B (OpenThinker-7B, trained on the OpenThoughts dataset~\citep{openthinker}; Qwen-7B backbone, STILL-trained, $n{=}47$), QwQ-32B (Qwen-32B, native reasoning, $n{=}19$--$20$), and R1-32B (Qwen-32B, R1-distilled, $n{=}20$). All traces come from HarmThoughts with step-level CP annotations (60/20/20 split). HS probes extract last-token hidden states from a selected layer; text probes encode each step with all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (384d). Both use L2-regularized logistic regression with temporal windowing $W \in \{1, 3, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25\}$ selected on validation. Detection requires $K{=}5$ consecutive threshold crossings. Statistical testing follows \cref{sec:evaluation}.
10	
11	\subsection{Layer Selection Results}\label{sec:layer-results}
12	
13	\cref{tab:layer_selection} shows that the crossing-rate composite metric (balanced accuracy $\times$ crossing rate) systematically selects shallow layers across all four models: L0 for R1-8B (full L0--L24 sweep; \cref{tab:r18b_full_layer}) and OT-7B, L2 (3\%) for QwQ-32B, and L10 (16\%) for R1-32B. The three threshold-based metrics (precision, inverse FPR, additive composite) share a common confusion matrix and empirically converge to the same deep layer---L63 (98\%) for both 32B models---consistent with their shared structure, though not mathematically guaranteed. Pure balanced accuracy, a threshold-free metric, selects layers that vary across data splits and models (7--98\% depth under 60/20/20; \cref{tab:ba_layer_comparison}), itself demonstrating that layer selection is a consequential methodological choice. The total exploration space spans 5 metrics $\times$ 7 window sizes $\times$ 28--64 layers (model-dependent); HB correction covers the final 12 model-metric tests, not this full search (\cref{app:hyperparameter_robustness}). The mechanism is that shallow layers produce highly compressed representations with small inter-step margins: step-to-step cosine distances are 1.4--2.7$\times$ smaller than at deep layers across all models (\cref{app:cosine_volatility}). A linear probe in this compressed space operates near the noise floor, generating frequent threshold crossings that inflate crossing rate independently of discriminative power (\cref{sec:layer-sensitivity}).\looseness=-1
14

17	\small

28	\caption{Layer selection sensitivity. $^a$\,Crossing-rate composite (bal\_acc $\times$ crossing\_rate). $^b$\,Consensus of threshold-based metrics (precision, inverse FPR, additive composite). Rightmost: HS vs.\ text precision $p$-value at threshold-based layer (e.g., QwQ-32B CR-composite layer: bal\_acc $p{=}0.35$, precision $p{=}0.83$, both non-significant).}
29	\label{tab:layer_selection}
30	\end{table}
31

The $\dagger$ marks sample-limited test sets ($n \leq 20$) where effect sizes are descriptive rather than confirmatory. Had we reported only CR-composite-layer results, we would have concluded a scale-dependent HS advantage that is entirely a methodological artifact. A random-label control on QwQ-32B confirms that the crossing-rate shallow-layer bias is a geometric property of the representations (100\% of random-label repeats select shallow layers), while threshold-based deep-layer selection requires real safety labels (\cref{app:random_cp}).
